verdict.summary: Facebook Login can be developed with app-role users, but production access beyond basic identity and Marketing API use can require App Review, business verification, and possibly Tech Provider access verification. Build a narrow, demonstrable flow and submit early; plan around an uncommitted review and verification timeline rather than a launch-date SLA.
verdict.activeEffort: Create and configure the app, build a working least-privilege OAuth and Marketing API flow, prepare review evidence, and complete any applicable business or Tech Provider verification.
verdict.waitTime: Unstated for App Review, business verification, and Tech Provider verification.
verdict.mainGate: App Review for non-basic Facebook Login permissions and applicable Marketing API access, with verification requirements depending on the requested access and business model.

steps.title: Create the Meta app in the developer dashboard

detail.text: Create and configure the app in the Meta for Developers dashboard.

steps.title: Determine whether the product serves other businesses

detail.text: An agent that serves other businesses using their assets should assess whether it is a Tech Provider and must complete the applicable access-verification flow; the trigger list includes several Marketing-API-related permissions.

sources.quote: permissions that can trigger this requirement, including several Marketing API-related permissions.

steps.title: Add Facebook Login and configure the exact callback

detail.text: Configure Facebook Login and its valid OAuth redirect URI before sending users through OAuth; use only an exact callback URL controlled by the application.

sources.quote: Covers Facebook Login setup and permission statuses such as ‘Ready for testing’ and ‘Ready for live mode.’

detail.text: Marketing API onboarding requires an app configuration and an active ad account.

sources.quote: including app configuration and an active ad account.

steps.title: Define the minimum permission and Marketing API access request

detail.text: Request only permissions used by the product, because permissions beyond public_profile and email generally require review before broader user access.

sources.quote: permissions beyond `public_profile` and `email` generally require review before broader user access.

steps.title: Assign real testers as app-role users

detail.text: During development, users listed in an app’s Roles section can grant valid permissions without Facebook approval.

sources.quote: users listed in an app’s Roles section can grant valid permissions during development without Facebook approval.

steps.title: Build and exercise the OAuth and requested API flows

detail.text: The OAuth authorize endpoint returned HTTP 200 in the recorded probe.

steps.title: Keep the app in development mode while testing

detail.text: Development Mode restricts permissions, features, discoverability, and generated data to users with app roles; production connections require Live Mode.

sources.quote: Development Mode restricts permissions, features, discoverability, and generated data to users with app roles; switch to Live Mode after development and App Review.

detail.text: Prepare reviewer access, a working test flow, and a screen recording that demonstrates each requested permission or feature.

sources.quote: submission requirements, including reviewer access, screen recordings, and demonstrations of each requested permission or feature.

steps.title: Complete the current review answers and submit

detail.text: The current review flow covers verification, app settings, allowed usage, data handling, data protection, and reviewer instructions.

sources.quote: the six required components of the updated review process: verification, app settings, allowed usage, data handling, data protection, and reviewer instructions.

steps.title: Complete business and access verification if applicable

detail.text: Connect the app to a verified Meta Business or Business Portfolio where verification is required, especially for apps requesting advanced access or serving other businesses.

sources.quote: Business Verification is required, especially for apps requesting advanced access or serving other businesses.

steps.title: Wait for review and answer requested changes

detail.text: No fixed App Review, business-verification, or Tech Provider-verification timeline is stated in the reviewed materials.

steps.title: Switch to Live Mode after approval

detail.text: Switch to Live Mode after development and App Review for production connections.

steps.title: Use current Marketing API access terminology in planning

detail.text: For Marketing API planning, use Limited and Full Marketing API Access terminology rather than older Standard and Advanced terminology.

sources.quote: the newer terminology change from Standard/Advanced Access to Limited/Full Marketing API Access tiers.

gotchas.text: Apps are limited to 10 test users, and Meta currently says creation of new test users is temporarily unavailable.

sources.quote: apps are limited to 10 test users, and Meta currently says creation of new test users is temporarily unavailable.

gotchas.text: Every requested permission or feature must be demonstrated in the submission materials.

sources.quote: every requested permission or feature must be demonstrated in the submission materials.

gotchas.text: Unapproved access is restricted to app-role users, while approved access is for everyone.

whenBlocked.text: If a review submission is rejected or blocked, reduce the request to product-used scopes and ensure each requested permission is separately demonstrated with working reviewer credentials and matching data-handling explanations.
If new test-user creation is unavailable, use existing eligible app-role users for development testing.
If serving other businesses or requesting access-verification-triggering Marketing API permissions, determine Tech Provider status and complete the applicable access-verification flow.

uncertain: The reviewed materials do not confirm an App Review, business-verification, or Tech Provider-verification SLA or review fee.

The general Graph API access-level page uses Standard and Advanced Access terminology, while newer Marketing API onboarding uses Limited and Full Marketing API Access; the evidence does not map every Marketing API permission or feature to a specific current tier.
The evidence does not identify which exact Marketing API permissions trigger Tech Provider access verification.
